english.title: Corruptly provide treat in form of meat, drink, entertainment, provision to influence voting at election
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of treating and therefore guilty of a corrupt practice in that you corruptly, before, during or after an election, namely **(..SPECIFY ELECTION,,), directly or indirectly

(A)_[gave or provided]_
(B)_[paid wholly or in part the expense of giving or providing]_

meat, drink, entertainment or provision to or for a person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..),

(C)_[for the purpose of corruptly influencing that or another person]_
(D)_[on account of that person or another person having voted or refrained from voting, or being about]_

to vote or refrain from voting
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 114(1) and (2) and 168(1) of the Representation of the People Act 1983
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
corruptly, either before, during or after an election
gives or provides or pays wholly or in part the expense of giving or providing
meat, drink, provision or entertainment to or for a person
for the purpose of corruptly influencing voting or the refrain from voting
or on account of a person having voted or refrained from voting or being about to do so

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum one years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
NoneNote
Note that for offences committed since 12 March 2015, section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012 removes the limits on certain fines given by the Magistrates' Courts. Offences that were previously punishable by fines of 'prescribed sums' and that were limited to 'not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale' or 'not exceeding the statutory maximum', are now punishable by a fine of any amount.
